question: Which Union Territory has the highest population density as per Census 2011?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, Delhi recorded the **highest population density among all Union Territories**, with 11,297 persons per square kilometer.
 
• Delhi’s population density is significantly higher compared to other Union Territories like Chandigarh (9,252) and Puducherry (2,547).
 
• The high population density in Delhi is attributed to its **status as India’s national capital**, with a large influx of migrants for employment, education, and better living standards.
 
• Delhi spans an area of 1,483 square kilometers and had a total population of over 16.78 million as per the 2011 Census.
 
• Population density is a critical indicator of urbanization, and Delhi’s figure highlights challenges like **infrastructure strain, traffic congestion, and pollution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density Definition:**

 
 
• Population density refers to the number of people living per unit area, typically measured in persons per square kilometer.
 
• It is an important metric for understanding urbanization, resource allocation, and development planning.
 
 
 
• **Other Densely Populated Union Territories:**
 
 
• Chandigarh ranks second among Union Territories in population density with 9,252 persons per square kilometer.
 
• Puducherry, another prominent Union Territory, has a population density of 2,547 persons per square kilometer.
 
 
 
• **India’s Average Population Density (2011):**
 
 
• India’s overall population density was 382 persons per square kilometer as per Census 2011.
 
• States like Bihar (1,106) and West Bengal (1,028) also recorded high population densities.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of High Population Density:**
 
 
• High population density leads to issues such as housing shortages, traffic congestion, pollution, and stress on public services.
 
• Proper urban planning and sustainable development are crucial to addressing these challenges.
